attempts.entry_title: Dopamine and spontaneous behaviour in the open field (Markowitz et al. 2023)
attempts.summary: The paper's links between striatal dopamine and syllable use held up in this data, but its central optogenetic learning result did not. Dopamine differed across syllables, syllables with more dopamine were used more, and larger transients predicted more use over the following minutes. Pairing a syllable with optogenetic dopamine release did not raise its use significantly over controls when the baseline was the day before stimulation; a later check with the Monday baseline of the paper's code gave the paper's result. The effects of stimulation on transition entropy and later predictability did not hold either. The food-reward and calibration sessions are missing from the dataset, and the decoding and reinforcement-learning models were not run for time.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Markowitz, Gillis, Jay et al. (2023) on dandiset 000559, which holds dLight photometry from the dorsolateral and dorsomedial striatum with MoSeq syllables, keypoint sessions, and closed-loop optogenetic (Opto-DA) experiments in Ai32 and no-opsin control mice. One notebook tests the photometry findings (dopamine at syllable transitions, its relation to velocity, syllable use and sequencing, DMS against DLS), the other the Opto-DA findings (reinforcement of the target syllable, learners, sequence entropy, kinematics, duration and place preference).

outcomes.statement: DLS dopamine fluctuations are significantly negatively correlated with translational velocity at short timescales (under 10 s), and the correlation reverses and becomes positive at longer timescales, for both dLight transient rates and binned amplitudes.
outcomes.source: Results, Relating DLS dopamine to spontaneous behavior, paragraph 2; Figure 1e
outcomes.quote: These dopamine fluctuations (measured as both dLight transient rates and average binned amplitudes) were only weakly correlated with many aspects of movement kinematics ... but were significantly negatively correlated with translational velocity at short timescales (<10 s); this correlation reversed and became positive at longer timescales
outcomes.notes: Transient rate (upward crossings of 1.96) holds under both readings of significance, significantly negative at all 20 bin sizes below 10 s and significantly positive at 73 (legend's per-bin test) or 27 (code's Holm test with runs of 5) of 100 bin sizes of 10 s or more, sign change near 16 s; with integer bin sizes 38 or 36 of 50. Binned amplitude is negative at every bin size (-0.119 at 0.25 s, -0.205 at 5.25 s, -0.051 at 59.75 s) and never significantly positive; the 1-s.d. rate is never significantly positive either. Without the 20-s sliding z-score neither measure is significantly positive at any bin size (amplitude -0.274, rate -0.166 at 59.75 s). Holds for one measure of two. Seed range not computed.
deviations: The DLS baseline set is the code's reading (the dLight+ChrimsonR mice's pure post days dropped), 164 experiments of 14 mice; the paper counts 216 experiments in Fig. 1b.
The code's two-sided test is computed from the z of the observed mean r against the 1,000 shuffles (normal approximation), as an empirical P from 1,000 shuffles cannot pass Holm over 120 bin sizes.
The 20-s sliding z-score is the Methods' pre-processing for all dLight (Photometry pre-processing); a variant without it is shown.
The five-seed range was not computed, for time.

outcomes.statement: In keypoint-tracked mice, 2D velocity is negatively correlated with dLight in 400-ms bins (r = -0.16), and forelimb velocity, with other kinematics partialled out, correlates only negligibly (r = -0.02).
outcomes.source: Extended Data Figure 3c; Results, Relating DLS dopamine to spontaneous behavior, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: correlation between 2D velocity and dLight fluorescence after binning the data into 400ms time points (Pearson r = −0.16, p < .001 one-sided shuffle test) ... (see Methods , Pearson r = −0.02, p < .001 one-sided shuffle test)
outcomes.notes: Five keypoint mice, 25-min sessions, 400-ms bins. The reader's answer (questions/markowitz-2023.yaml) amended the criterion to process dLight with the Methods' RANSAC fit with slope and bias, the main reading of the claims file's definitions, and made the fig_s03 notebook's fit without intercept a variant. Under the amended criterion 2D velocity and dLight correlate at r = -0.170 pooled (per-mouse mean -0.169, mice -0.128 to -0.220; one-sided shuffle P = 0.001 under all five seeds), within -0.16 +- 0.016, and forelimb velocity and partialled dLight at r = -0.026 pooled (per-mouse mean -0.027; P = 0.001, 0.001 to 0.002 over the five seeds), outside -0.02 +- 0.002 under both readings and rounding to -0.03, so one expected value of two is met. With the fit without intercept, on which the round-2 outcome (reproduced) rested, the values are -0.167 and -0.019 (P = 0.001 and 0.002), both within tolerance. Changed to partially reproduced in round 3. Photometry and keypoint series start at 0 s, have equal lengths in every session and share the 30-Hz rate.

Keypoints and photometry are paired by sample index; the files give both series a start at 0 s, equal lengths and a 30-Hz rate, and no other alignment.

outcomes.statement: The average syllable-associated dLight transient exceeds that associated with movement initiation (P = 0.0006, n = 14 mice).
outcomes.source: Figure 1f legend
outcomes.quote: The average syllable-associated dLight transient exceeds that associated with movement initiation
outcomes.notes: Movement initiations are the changepoint-score peaks (derivative per second), all detections (25 to 30 per minute, mean speed in the second before 43 to 77 mm/s) or those preceded by relative stillness (2.3 to 5.5 per minute, speed rising from 12 to 27 mm/s before to 55 to 107 mm/s after). With initiations from stillness, reading (a), the mean absolute z of 1-Hz high-passed snippets from -1 to +1 s, favours syllable onsets in 13 of 14 mice (medians 2.25 against 1.17, P = 0.00024) and reading (b), the peak from 0 to 0.3 s, does not (9 of 14, P = 0.36). With all detections, the criterion's definition, (b) favours syllables (13 of 14, P = 0.00024, also with 100 shuffles and under quality control (b)) and (a) favours movement (3 of 14, P = 0.004). Syllable onsets outnumber initiations from stillness about 30 to 1, and the shuffle z grows with the event count. With syllable onsets drawn down to each mouse's initiation count (100 shuffles), against initiations from stillness reading (a) has syllables higher in 5 of 14 (P = 0.068) under the claim's seed and in 2 to 4 of 14 (P 0.0023 to 0.013, favouring movement) under seeds +1000 to +4000, and reading (b) shows no difference (6 to 10 of 14, P 0.27 to 0.90); against all detections, (b) favours syllables in 14 of 14 and (a) favours movement in 14 of 14 (P = 0.00012 under all five seeds). The round-2 outcome (reproduced) rested on reading (a) with initiations from stillness, which the count-matched check removes; under the criterion's definition (b) meets the rule and (a) is significant the other way, so the claim holds in part (changed to partially reproduced in round 3). The 6 dLight-only mice have higher reading (b) syllable peaks than the 8 dLight+ChrimsonR mice (medians 3.83 and -0.10, U = 48 of 48, P = 0.001); in them alone (b) favours syllables in 6 of 6 under both definitions (P = 0.031).
deviations: The DLS baseline set is the code's reading, 164 experiments of 14 mice; the paper counts 216 in Fig. 1b.

Movement initiations use the derivative of the smoothed z-scored speed per second; per frame the cubed score never reaches the find_peaks height of 1. A variant keeps those preceded by relative stillness (mean smoothed speed in the second before below the experiment's 25th percentile), as the Methods describe the events ("moments where mice transitioned from periods of relative stillness to movement"); the percentile is an assumption.

Reading (a) uses 100 shuffles (the legend's number) and a second-order Butterworth high-pass, a standard choice; reading (b) 1,000 and 100. The count-matched check uses 100 shuffles for the drawn syllable onsets.

outcomes.statement: Random forest classifiers cannot predict which syllable is being expressed from the coincident dLight peak amplitude or waveform.
outcomes.source: Results, DLS dopamine does not predict syllable identity, paragraph 2; Figure 1l
outcomes.quote: Indeed, random forest classifiers were unable to predict which syllable was being expressed by the mouse at any moment based on the coincident dLight waveform amplitudes or shapes

outcomes.statement: The dLight autocorrelation and the dLight-velocity correlation decline sharply within a few hundred milliseconds, so they do not explain the dLight-usage relationship.
outcomes.source: Results, Dopamine predicts future syllable use and sequencing, paragraph 2; Figure 2e

outcomes.notes: The reader's answer (questions/markowitz-2023.yaml) amended the criterion to the Fig. 2e legend's one-sided test for all three curves, a curve counting as declined at n when it is not significantly positive there, and added a partially reproduced case; the bins stay those of the figure. The usage correlation is significant at every n from 10 to 390 (P = 0.001). The autocorrelation is significantly positive at n = 10 (z 5.63, P = 0.001) and declined from n = 30 on (z -1.16 to -4.34). The velocity curve is declined at n = 10 (z -11.73) and significantly positive at every n from 30 to 390 (z 0.85 to 2.18, P 0.001 to 0.046). No n has both declined and neither curve is significantly positive at every n, so the criterion's partial case applies. Under the seeds plus 1000 and 2000 the outcome is the same (velocity P at n = 390 0.049 and 0.038); under the seeds plus 3000 and 4000 the velocity curve is not significant at n = 390 (P 0.079 and 0.054), both curves are declined there and the outcome would be reproduced. Before the answer the outcome was the same, as a judgment between two cases that did not cover the result; the answer makes it the criterion's own case, so it no longer rests on an assumption.

The seed range reruns the shuffles of fig2e-dlight-predicts-future-usage, whose generator the criterion shares, under its seed plus 1000 to 4000.

findings.statement: The food-reward photometry experiments (Methods, 6 mice), the open-loop dLight calibration experiments (2 dLight+ChrimsonR mice) and the dLight+ChrimsonR closed-loop sessions with 2-s and 3-s stimulation are not in the dandiset; only two 2-s excitation sessions of the dLight+ChrimsonR mice are. The release notes of 0.261113.1911 state the first and last are missing.

The dandiset holds 10 DMS mice where the paper reports 8; dms-dlight-7 and dms-dlight-9 have no photometry. Of the photometry session files, 92 of 167 DMS and 22 of 97 dLight-only DLS files, and 10 of 236 dLight+ChrimsonR files, have behaviour but no photometry series, without a note saying why. dls-dlight-6 and dls-dlight-8 have no photometry, consistent with the two mice the paper excluded.

The DLS photometry experiments without stimulation number 164 (dLight-only mice and the dLight+ChrimsonR files that are a baseline day of some target) or 204 with the pure post-stimulation days, against 216 in Fig. 1b and 378 baseline experiments in the Methods. The DMS experiments with photometry number 75 under the Methods' quality control and 64 under the code's rule, which matches the paper. Which files form the paper's DLS sets is not recorded. 38 dLight+ChrimsonR files are the baseline day of one target and the post day of another (two rows of their TargetSessions table), and two 2-s excitation sessions carry session numbers 0 and 4, those of a baseline and a post day.
The OptogeneticSeries description says onsets are recorded as 1 and offsets as 0, but the onset values are the power, 0.01 W.
Over the stimulation files 70.7% of target detections are stimulated, where the Methods give 75%.

One dLight+ChrimsonR session of dlight-chrimson-6 has a dF/F of up to 10,804% and a dLight-reference correlation of 0.998, and is not marked excluded in its TargetSessions table; it fails the Methods' quality control. One dls-dlight-7 session has a raw dF/F of up to 228 (22,798%); it passes the Methods' rule and fails the code's.

The keypoint files give the keypoint reference frame as 'TBD', hold raw fluorescence without timestamps linking it to the keypoints other than a shared start at 0 s and equal lengths at 30 Hz, and their sessions last 25 min.

The velocity-modulation files do not record whether stimulation targeted the fastest or the slowest quartile of the target's velocity, except in the session descriptions of mice 5891 to 5894 ('Stim session -up', '-down'); the five dls-ai32jr mice's 50 files and the remaining files of the other four mice do not say. The dandiset has 9 mice with such files, the paper 5. The direction can be read from the velocities of the stimulated instances once their detection times are corrected (next finding); this agrees with the stated direction in 16 of 17 files.

In the velocity-modulation files the TargetDetections times and the OptogeneticSeries light onsets are 2700.03 s later than the clock of the syllable labels and the other behavioural series. 2,845 of 3,423 detections and 1,901 of 2,479 light onsets fall after the last syllable onset of their file, and 1.0% of detections fall on an instance of the target syllable; shifted by -2700.03 s, 99.4% do. In the reinforcement files the detections fall on target instances without a shift (median 99.7%).

The syllable-onset dLight averages differ between the two DLS groups. The peak of the shuffle-normalised average from 0 to 0.3 s has a median of 3.83 in the 6 dLight-only mice and -0.10 in the 8 dLight+ChrimsonR mice (reinforcement-photometry files; U = 48 of 48, P = 0.001), and the average reaches its maximum within 0 to +1 s at 0.30 to 0.33 s in every dLight-only mouse but at 0.97 to 1.0 s in 5 of the 8 dLight+ChrimsonR mice. A label shift check gives the same best shift (-3 samples) in both groups, so a clock offset does not explain it, and the files do not say what else differs.

The re-referenced, z-scored dLight trace that the paper's photometry analyses use is not stored, nor the fit of the reference behind it. The 376 files with a dLight dF/F series hold the dLight and reference dF/F, the smoothed references and, in 363, the raw photometry, so the trace has to be recomputed from the Methods.

outcomes.note: The earlier criterion, written by that attempt's author, used a 100-tree forest and called identity not decodable below twice chance (0.0541), which 0.0271 and 0.0323 met. The new criterion asks for the paper's forest of 1,000 trees and 100 label shuffles, which this attempt estimated at about 83 h and 238 h and blocked as too_large without running.

The earlier criterion used five equal 360-s segments, r per experiment and syllable, and raw r against shuffles, and failed at n = 110 to 170 (P = 0.09, 0.15, 0.18 and 0.05). The new criterion takes the paper's segments, pools a mouse's experiments and z-scores r against shuffles per segment, and is significant at every n from 10 to 390 (z 7.00 at n = 10, 2.25 at 170).

The earlier criterion applied the Fig. 2e lagged test to DMS, which was significant at 9 of 10 values of n. The new criterion is the encoding-model comparison of Extended Data Fig. 7e and depends on ed6b-encoding-model-average, which this attempt did not run, so it is blocked with it.

The earlier criterion took the latest Monday baseline day up to five days before stimulation, as the paper's code does (U = 198, P = 0.0013); the new one takes the most recent previous baseline day, with the Monday rule as a variant (U = 152, P = 0.110). The new attempt's Monday variant (optoda.ipynb, cell 4, target_table) looks for a Monday only among the target's own baseline rows, so it changed none of the 191 baselines and does not test the code's rule.

The same change of baseline day as for fig3e-optoda-learning. With the Monday baseline the earlier attempt found U = 182, P = 0.0083 (control median -2.3); with the day before, this attempt found U = 160, P = 0.062 (control median 23.2).

Both attempts find the learners correlated (r = 0.891 and 0.868, n = 7) and the controls correlated too (r = 0.591, P = 0.017 and r = 0.633, P = 0.025, where the paper reports P = 0.082). The new criterion adds that the controls must not be significant, so the same result is partially reproduced under it.

Version 0.260528.0858 did not mark catch trials, so the earlier attempt could not run the test; 0.261113.1911 marks them in TargetDetections, and this attempt ran it on 377 experiments. Its outcome rests on an assumption, stimulation trials drawn down to the catch count (Opto-DA first bin Holm P = 0.86); with all trials the Opto-DA first bin has Holm P = 0.017.

Without catch trials in 0.260528.0858 the earlier attempt used substitute ones, which differed from stimulation trials in 9 of 12 no-opsin controls, and blocked the claim. With the catch trials of 0.261113.1911 this attempt finds no Opto-DA bin significant for any variable (Holm P 1.0, f 0.46 to 0.53).

As for fig3l-no-kinematic-effect, the earlier substitute catch trials gave significant differences in both controls and the claim was blocked. With the catch trials of 0.261113.1911 every Opto-DA bin has Holm P 1.0 in 36 experiments of 3 mice; the earlier variant with catch trials at least 2 s from any pulse also found 0 of 3 Opto-DA mice significant.

The earlier claims file gave this claim no criterion, and that attempt did not run it, for time, though the data were in its version. The new claims file gives two readings, and this attempt found they disagree (with all detections, 13 of 14 mice favour syllable onsets under one and 3 of 14 under the other).

The earlier claims file gave this claim no criterion, and that attempt did not run it, for time. This attempt tested it under the new criterion after its first verification round, positive under reading (a) (Pearson z 1.24 and 1.93, P = 0.003 and 0.001 at n = 5 and 10) and negative under reading (b).

The earlier claims file gave this claim no criterion, and that attempt did not run it, for time; the light onsets of the velocity-modulation files and the missing up or down labels are the same in both versions. This attempt ran the new criterion with the direction read from velocity where the files do not state it (11 up and 6 down experiments, P = 0.180).

disagreements.reason: Reading (b) gives syllable > movement in 14/14 mice, P = 0.00012, which meets the criterion. Reading (a) is significant the other way (P = 0.011). Reading (b) wins only because the movement-aligned averages are deep dips in every mouse. movement_onsets multiplies the derivative by FS before cubing; on synthetic noise this yields about 1,400 initiations per 30 min, the data about 700 per experiment, and these are not the Methods' stillness-to-movement transitions.

Reading (a) gives P = 0.10. Reading (b) gives P = 0.039 (0.034-0.054 over seeds), which nominally meets the partial rule, but that P is uncorrected for picking the peak among 31 lags, and its null is miscalibrated, as permuting dLight across overlapping windows destroys the autocorrelation that the observed curve keeps.
Main reading (post day), the top-rank 95% bootstrap intervals include 0 (inbound -0.05 to 0.77, outbound -0.13 to 0.55). Only the stimulation-day variant meets the rule.

Under the criterion's two tests, by pair (P = 0.31) and by mouse (P = 0.52), it is reproduced. The notebook's experiment-wide test, closer to the paper's "experiment-wide" statistic, gives P = 0.005, with Opto-DA JSD lower than controls (f = 0.20). The claims file reads the experiment-wide statistic as per-mouse means of the target-onset JSD, a misreading; the experiment-wide result suggests a rig or coordinate difference between groups that was never checked. jsd returns a negative value, not NaN, when one histogram is empty.

paper_notes.statement: Question for the authors. Movement initiations (Methods, Movement initiation analyses) are peaks of the cubed derivative of the smoothed z-scored speed with height 1. Taking the derivative per frame gives no peak above 1 in these data; per second gives 25 to 30 a minute, mostly during movement. Which units were used, and were the events restricted to starts from stillness, as the Methods' description says? This attempt used per second and kept detections preceded by speed below the experiment's 25th percentile.

Question for the authors. For Fig. 1f, what quantity is compared between syllable onsets and movement initiations, and were the event counts matched? Syllable onsets outnumber initiations about 4 to 1 (all detections) or 30 to 1 (from stillness), and the shuffle-normalised z grows with the count. With counts matched, the peak of the shuffle-normalised average from 0 to 0.3 s favours syllable onsets over all detections in 14 of 14 mice, while the mean absolute z of 1-Hz high-passed snippets from -1 to +1 s, as the fig_1f notebook computes, favours movement initiations in 14 of 14.

Question for the authors. For Fig. 3i, is the post-onset transition entropy computed per trial or pooled over a condition's trials, and are stimulation and catch trials matched in number? Stimulation trials are about three times as many as catch trials; pooled, the Opto-DA effect is significant, and with stimulation trials drawn down to the catch count it is not.

Question for the authors. For Extended Data Fig. 10d, which experiments form the baseline of the inclusion rule ("separate recording experiments with no stimulation"), and how was the direction of each velocity-modulation experiment recorded? This attempt read the direction from the stimulated instances' velocities where the files do not state it, and took as baseline the mouse's velocity-modulation files without stimulation; with these choices up does not exceed down significantly (11 up and 6 down experiments, P = 0.180).

entries.title: Dopamine and spontaneous behaviour in the open field (Markowitz et al. 2023)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Markowitz, Gillis, Jay et al. (2023) on dandiset 000559, which holds dLight photometry from the dorsolateral and dorsomedial striatum with MoSeq syllables, keypoint sessions, and closed-loop optogenetic (Opto-DA) experiments in Ai32 and no-opsin control mice. One notebook tests the photometry findings (dopamine at syllable transitions, its relation to velocity, syllable use and sequencing, DMS against DLS), the other the Opto-DA findings (reinforcement of the target syllable, learners, sequence entropy, kinematics, duration and place preference).
